proposed_facts.reason: Canonical lines 129-153 confirm attachment and channel guards, incremental validation and mutation, no rollback on an invalid link, and unconditional updater invocation after traversal, including an initial 0xFFFF.

Canonical lines 155-168 confirm metadata preparation and callback storage before the direct erase-start return. Lines 14-78 independently confirm currentFat re-fetch, negative-result terminal branches, nonnegative-write-only buffer rotation, guarded release, and clear-before-call completion.

Canonical lines 14-168 support the unit summary's mutation ordering and distinct synchronous initiation versus asynchronous completion paths. The rendered names are unchanged and fit these roles. Existing retained knowledge is inherited unchanged; no compiled-layout or universal recovery claim is needed.

contradictions.reason: The free-block supersession is justified: corruption can be detected after earlier entries and the free count have changed, and an initial terminator still reaches persistence. The proposed explanation preserves the supported existing guards.

The updater supersession correctly replaces an unqualified failure-completion interpretation. Initial erase-start failure is returned directly without local cleanup, whereas callback errors use explicit terminal paths. System-wide recovery and enforcement of the asynchronous currentFat lifetime are accepted deferrals, not inferred guarantees.

The unit-level supersession is supported: allocation reserves capacity before scanning, freeing mutates incrementally, and negative callback completion does not undo prior RAM changes. The functionality document and proposal consistently avoid implying transactional recovery.

unresolved: Accepted deferral: system-wide cleanup after an initial erase-start failure and enforcement of the currentFat asynchronous lifetime invariant remain unestablished. Acceptance covers the proposed changes and examined contradictions, not a new independent audit of inherited retained facts and links.
